semantic_classification: virtual update step that returns false when it has just released a completed owned target, and otherwise resolves a world position from the receiver's position source, pushes it into the owned target's emitter and commits an anchor position on the owned target before returning true

observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: AL only. The success exit writes AL=1 with MOV AL,0x1 at 0x01053ec4 and the failure exit writes AL=0 with XOR AL,AL at 0x01053ecd; the upper three bytes of EAX are never written on either path, so the machine produces a one-byte zero or one. The live Ghidra prototype is the placeholder `undefined FUN_01053e00(void)` and the SDK symbol table has no name for this address, so no declared return type exists to corroborate bool; bool is chosen because it is the type the machine's AL-only production supports and the type the staged span declares.
observed_original_abi.calling_convention: Observed MSVC x86 virtual-member convention already established for this table by the sibling reconstruction of 0x01053db0: the receiver is NOT in ECX but is the first callee-popped stack argument, read as MOV ESI,[ESP+0x20] at 0x01053e04 after SUB ESP,0x18 / PUSH ESI. ECX is used only to carry the receiver of each inner virtual.

observed_original_abi.frame: SUB ESP,0x18 / PUSH ESI at 0x01053e00-0x01053e03; POP ESI / ADD ESP,0x18 / RET 0x8 on both exits at 0x01053ec6-0x01053eca and 0x01053ecf-0x01053ed3. ESI is the only callee-saved register touched.
observed_original_abi.callee_cleanup_convention: The single POP ESI / ADD ESP,0x18 epilogue is only stack-balanced if all four inner calls remove their own pushed argument. That is the reading adopted here: the two zero-argument virtuals (words at +0x2c and +0x04 of the owned target, and the word at +0x2c of the position source) are entered with no push, and the four one-argument calls each push exactly one dword. Any other assignment leaves ESP off by four or eight bytes at the RET, which would fault on return.
observed_original_abi.correction_of_live_prototype: The live signature `undefined FUN_01053e00(void)` is a placeholder with no parameters; the body demonstrably consumes two callee-popped stack words and returns a byte in AL.

The vector is taken from the pointer the call RETURNED, not from the buffer passed to the slot +0x30 call: the machine never reads back the frame bytes written at [ESP+0x10], [ESP+0x14] or [ESP+0x18].
The three stores form a 12-byte copy; 0x01053ead re-takes its address with LEA EDX,[ESP+0x4] and passes it to the emitter.

0x01053ea8/0x01053eaa load the object stored at that field and take its vtable word at +0x38 into EAX; 0x01053eb1/0x01053eb2 call it with the copied vector as the single stack argument.

vtable_evidence.caveat: The region interleaves non-code words among the code pointers (0x00c6a960 at 0x0149b828 and 0x007b86e0 at 0x0149b82c, both confirmed by ghidra_read_memory), and SporeApp.exe carries no MSVC RTTI, so no complete-object locator confirms a base and no exact slot index is claimed. unresolved_questions: The function is unnamed in the image. FUN_01053e00 is the live Ghidra name, the Spore-ModAPI symbol table has no entry for this address, and the two SDK-named neighbours 0x01053d00 and 0x01053db0 are the only members carrying the cDefaultBeamTool this type. The class attribution is therefore evidence-based but the member or interface name is not recoverable and has not been invented.

The slot index of this entry is not established. It sits five words after the SDK-named func4Ch word in the tables based at 0x0149b810, 0x0149b900 and 0x0149ba30, but those regions interleave non-code words and the image has no RTTI, so the deltas are reported rather than a slot number.

Whether the second callee-popped stack word is a distinct 4-byte argument or the low half of a single 8-byte argument cannot be decided from `ret 8` alone. No instruction reads it, so it is staged as an opaque void* and never dereferenced.

The 12-byte buffer passed to the found object's vtable word at +0x30 is written by the callee but never read back by this body, which consumes the returned pointer instead. Whether that buffer is a genuine second output or a compiler artifact of the callee's prototype is not resolvable from this function alone.

The semantic role of each dispatched slot is inferred from shape only: the +0x2c query on the owned target, the +0xb8 keyed lookup, the +0x30 and +0x2c position accessors and the +0x38 emitter setter. No slot body is resolved in this package.

The commit helper 0x00cb5930 uses this function's own receiver word as a fallback pointer to three floats, which reads the first twelve bytes of the receiver object. That is what the listing does and it is staged verbatim, but it looks like an argument mix-up in the original; whether the caller ever reaches that fallback is unknown.

The eight code pointers stored at 0x013f94d4 are recorded as observed bytes but are deliberately left unspecified in the staged table, so no constant is asserted that the listing for this VA does not contain.
